Techniques Used: Gluing results for moduli of local systems
Data & Platforms: Root of unity quantum cluster algebras
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Non-commutative Geometric Resolution: Constructing endomorphism rings of conic modules over toric varieties to establish finite global dimension and characterize non-commutative crepant resolutions based on simpliciality.

Topological Combinatorial Parametrization: Defining the superunitary region of cluster algebras as a regular CW complex homeomorphic to the generalized associahedron to prove finiteness of positive integral friezes via compactness arguments.

Poisson-Quantum Duality Analysis: Linking the Zariski open orbits of symplectic leaves in classical upper cluster algebras to the Azumaya loci in their root of unity quantizations to bridge classical geometry with quantum representation theory.

Theta Function Basis Construction: Utilizing positive scattering diagrams to generate theta functions that satisfy valuative independence and reciprocity, thereby establishing linear independence and identifying bases for global sections on partial compactifications.
Summary Description: Greg Muller is a mathematician specializing in the intersection of commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, and representation theory, with a focus on cluster algebras and non-commutative resolutions. His work systematically bridges combinatorial structures with geometric and topological properties, utilizing tools such as conic modules, scattering diagrams, and CW complexes. Key contributions include characterizing non-commutative crepant resolutions via toric varieties, proving the topological structure of cluster algebras through the generalized associahedron, and establishing theta function bases for cluster varieties. His research provides deep insights into the singularities of algebraic varieties, the representation theory of quantum algebras, and the combinatorial classification of friezes, significantly advancing the understanding of the geometric and algebraic interplay in modern mathematical physics and algebra.
